Report_ID: Live birth (Delivery, n) per woman randomised/analysed
Title: Effects of transdermal testosterone application on the ovarian response to FSH in poor responders undergoing assisted reproduction technique—a prospective, randomized, double-blind study
Author: Massin, N.; Cedrin-Durnerin, I.; Coussieu, C.; Galey-Fontaine, J.; Wolf, J.P.; Hugues, J.-N.
Comment: No statistical test was performed for delivery; the paper states the low number of patients precluded any statistical comparison of pregnancy outcomes. Delivery counts are taken from the treated cycle (TC) column of each arm; denominators are the final analysed Ns (25 placebo, 24 testosterone), not the randomised Ns (26 and 27).
Participant type: Women aged ≤42 with previous poor ovarian response and decreased ovarian reserve undergoing a second IVF/ICSI cycle
Recruitment source: Reproductive Medicine Unit, Jean Verdier Hospital, University Paris XIII, Bondy, France (Oct 2001–Dec 2003)
Outcome measurement: Number of women with a delivery in the treated cycle, out of women analysed in each arm (25 placebo, 24 testosterone)
Outcome variable: Live birth (Delivery, n) per woman randomised/analysed
effect_direction: favors testosterone (2/24 vs 1/25), not statistically tested

Report_ID: Ongoing pregnancy per woman randomised (clinical pregnancies minus miscarriages; live birth not reported)
Title: Transdermal testosterone may improve ovarian response to gonadotrophins in low-responder IVF patients: a randomized, clinical trial
Author: Fàbregues et al.
Comment: Live birth not reported. Ongoing pregnancy event counts derived by subtracting the explicitly reported miscarriages (1 per group) from the explicitly reported clinical pregnancies (6 vs 4): 5/31 vs 3/31. The P-value 0.31 reported in the table refers to clinical pregnancy per started cycle, not to the derived ongoing pregnancy counts, so it is not attached here. Control arm is an active comparator (high-dose gonadotrophin + minidose GnRH agonist), not placebo/no pretreatment.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group 1: transdermal testosterone patch (20 µg/kg/day, 5 days) before standard r-hFSH stimulation') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: infertile women aged 31-39 with a previous IVF cycle cancelled for poor follicular response (low responders)
Recruitment source: Fertility unit, Hospital Clínic, University of Barcelona (September 2006 - July 2007)
Outcome measurement: Clinical pregnancies per started cycle: 6 (19.3%) in Group 1 vs 4 (12.9%) in Group 2; miscarriages 1 in each group, giving 5/31 vs 3/31 ongoing pregnancies
Outcome variable: Ongoing pregnancy per woman randomised (clinical pregnancies minus miscarriages; live birth not reported)
unit_of_analysis: per started cycle (= per woman randomised)

Title: Transdermal testosterone pretreatment in poor responders undergoing ICSI: a randomized clinical trial
Author: Bosdou et al.
Comment: Rate difference reported in text with OCR-corrupted minus signs ("20.6%", "219.0") corresponding to Table IV's "-0.6, -19.0 to +16.9". No odds ratio reported by the paper; only event counts and Fisher's exact P extracted. Study explicitly underpowered for live birth.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Transdermal testosterone pretreatment (10 mg/day gel, 21 days)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Women with poor ovarian response (Bologna criteria) undergoing ICSI
Recruitment source: Unit for Human Reproduction, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki and University of Thessaly fertility clinics
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of randomized women achieving a live birth
effect_direction: essentially null / marginally favors control (7.7% vs 8.3%, P=1.00)

Report_ID: Live birth rate per cycle initiated
Title: The effect of transdermal testosterone gel pretreatment on controlled ovarian stimulation and IVF outcome in low responders
Author: Kim, Howles, & Lee
Comment: Paper reports only event counts and a chi-square/Fisher p value; no odds ratio or confidence interval is reported. Live birth 'per cycle initiated' equals per woman randomised because 55 initiated cycles corresponded to 55 patients in each arm.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('TTG pretreatment (12.5 mg transdermal testosterone gel daily for 21 days before COS)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Low responder women undergoing IVF/ICSI (≤3 follicles ≥16 mm and ≤3 oocytes retrieved despite >2,500 IU gonadotropin in a previous failed cycle)
Recruitment source: University-based infertility clinic, Asan Medical Center, Seoul, South Korea, March 2005 – January 2009
Outcome measurement: Number of women with a live birth / number of cycles initiated (= women randomised) per arm
Outcome variable: Live birth rate per cycle initiated
unit_of_analysis: per cycle initiated (= per woman randomised, 55 cycles = 55 patients per arm)

Title: The Effect of Transdermal Testosterone Gel Pretreatment on IVF Outcomes in Patients with Poor Ovarian Reserve
Author: Sharma N, Nayar KD
Comment: Live birth not reported; ongoing pregnancy used as substitute. The Results prose gives slightly different figures for ongoing pregnancy ("27.5% vs 22.9%, p = 0.45") that conflict with Table 3; Table 3's counts (15/46 = 32.6%, 10/41 = 24.4%) are internally consistent and were extracted. Note also that the Abstract reverses the group sizes (41 TTG / 46 control) relative to the Results and all tables (46 TTG / 41 control).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Transdermal testosterone gel (TTG) 12.5 mg/day') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Women with diminished ovarian reserve (POSEIDON groups 3 and 4; AFC ≤5, AMH ≤1.2 ng/mL) undergoing IVF
Recruitment source: Akanksha IVF Centre, Mata Chanan Devi Hospital, Janakpuri, New Delhi, India
Outcome measurement: Number of women with ongoing pregnancy / number of women per arm
effect_direction: favors testosterone (32.6% vs 24.4%, P=0.39, not significant)

Title: Role of transdermal testosterone gel pre-treatment on IVF outcome: a prospective randomized controlled trial with active control
Author: Singh N, Parimalam P, Kumar S, Vanamail P
Comment: Table 2 header states N=35 for both groups, but the reported 14.7% corresponds to 5/34 (34 women in the study arm were analysed for pregnancy outcomes after one woman's transfer was deferred for OHSS risk); totals recorded as randomised N=35 per the synthesis plan's 'per woman randomised' rule. No effect measure (OR/RR) was reported by the paper.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Testosterone group (transdermal testosterone gel 1%, 12.5 mg/day pretreatment)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial with active control
Participant type: Women ≤39 years with previous failed IVF/ICSI cycle and ≤5 oocytes retrieved (unexpected poor ovarian responders) with normal ovarian reserve and normal or low testosterone
Recruitment source: ART Centre, Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, AIIMS, New Delhi
Outcome measurement: Number of women with a live birth per arm (dichotomous event counts)
effect_direction: favors testosterone (14.7% vs 2.9%, P=0.092, not significant)

Title: e2ebedb0_PIIS0015028210017279 — P-214: Ovarian features after 2 weeks, 3 weeks and 4 weeks transdermal testosterone gel treatment and their associated effect on IVF/ICSI outcome in low responders
Author: C.-H. Kim, J.-W. Ahn, H.-Y. Nah, S.-H. Kim, H.-D. Chae, B.-M. Kang
Comment: No usable numeric data: the abstract reports only the qualitative statement "similar to those in control group" for the 2-week TTG arm. Live birth and ongoing pregnancy are not reported at all — only clinical pregnancy rate per cycle initiated, which is a proxy the synthesis plan does not pool. additional_group_ns: Trial randomised 120 low responders into 4 arms (control, 2-week TTG, 3-week TTG, 4-week TTG); per-arm sample sizes are NOT reported. The 3-week and 4-week TTG arms are recorded as separate rows.

Report_ID: Ongoing pregnancy rate (%) — live birth proxy
Title: Therapeutic effect of prolonged testosterone pretreatment in women with poor ovarian response: A randomized control trial
Author: Hoang QH, Ho HS, Do HT, Nguyen TV, Nguyen HP, Le MT
Comment: Chi-square P for the 4 wk vs control comparison is reported as .00 (Table 3, P2); the OR 5.84 is adjusted for maternal age, BMI, infertility duration, infertility type and IVF history (Table 4), not a crude OR. Denominators are cycles with oocyte retrieval/embryo transfer (40/40), not the randomised Ns (42/42). The control group is shared with the 6 wk arm and is NOT split here — raw counts recorded as printed; downstream splitting is required to avoid double-counting controls.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('4 wk transdermal testosterone gel (12.5 mg/day) pretreatment') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Infertile women with poor ovarian response (Bologna criteria) undergoing IVF
Recruitment source: National Center for Reproductive Medicine, Hanoi, Vietnam (Jan 2018 - Sep 2019)
Outcome measurement: Number of women with a viable intrauterine pregnancy after 12 weeks of gestation, per cycle with oocyte retrieval and embryo transfer (n = 40 per arm)
Outcome variable: Ongoing pregnancy rate (%) — live birth proxy
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used in this row: 6 wk TTG group, 8/37 (21.6%) ongoing pregnancies (extracted as a separate row); randomised Ns were 42 (4 wk), 42 (control), 38 (6 wk)
effect_direction: favors testosterone (30.0% vs 7.5%; adjusted OR 5.84, 95% CI 1.36-25.1, P=.02)
unit_of_analysis: per cycle with oocyte retrieval and embryo transfer (n=40 per arm)
